#Part 1
1.Open the sleep dataset in R
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
data(sleep)
```

2. Is it long or wide format? How do you know?
**It's long data. Each participant only has 2 rows of data showing the results of the two different types of drugs used, as apposed to having each participant having 1 row with the results in separate columns. **

3. Transform this data so that it is in the other format.
```{r}
sleepWide<- sleep |> pivot_wider (id_cols=c("ID"), names_from="group", values_from="extra", names_prefix="group ")
```

4. Transform your data back to its original format.
```{r}
sleepLong<- sleepWide |> pivot_longer(cols=c("group 1", "group 2"), names_to="participant", values_to="extra")
```

5. Open the Starwars dataset
```{r}
data(starwars)
```


6. Create homeworld as a factor. How many levels does it have?
```{r}
starwars$homeworldFactors<- as.factor(starwars$homeworld)
#48 levels
```

7. Reorder homeworld so that Naboo is the reference group.
```{r}
starwars$homeworldFactors<- relevel(starwars$homeworldFactors, ref= "Naboo")
print(starwars$homeworldFactors)
```

8. Use mutate to create a column transforming kg to pounds. (hint: you may need to look up the conversion)
```{r}
newWeight<-starwars |> mutate(massLBS=mass*2.205) |> select(mass, massLBS)
```

9. Print a summary of your column from #8
```{r}
summary(newWeight)
```


#Part 2
10. open the billboard dataset.
```{r}
data("billboard")
```

11. are the data in this dataframe in long or wide format? explain how you know.
```{r}
#Wide. One row per song.
```

12. change the data from its original format to the other version.
```{r}
billboardLong<- billboard |> pivot_longer(cols= c(colnames(billboard)[4:79]), names_to= "weeks", values_to="position", values_drop_na = TRUE)
```

13. change it from your altered version in #3 back to its original state.
```{r}
billboardWide<- billboardLong |> pivot_wider(id_cols=c("artist", "track", "date.entered"), names_from="weeks", values_from="position")
```

14. Separate the date entered column into three columns: one for year, one for month, and one for day.
```{r}
billboardNewDateFormat<- billboard |> separate(date.entered, into=c("year", "month", "day"), sep="-")
```
